subject: Discovery recap — inference economics, caching/batching expectations & quantization tolerance
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@corelytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap — inference economics, caching/batching expectations & quantization tolerance

Hi Sam / Maya,

Thanks again for your time today — good conversation. Below is a short recap so we have aligned next steps and success criteria before the technical follow-up.

Quick summary of pain points you shared:
- Unit economics: production inference spend has grown ~3x YoY; current per-request token cost is the primary stopgap for new feature launches.
- Tail latency spikes: occasional P95/P99s that impact user flows (search and realtime suggestions).
- Limited caching: current stack has minimal prefix caching; most requests hit the model cold.
- Batching constraints: front-end concurrency patterns make large batch windows impractical today.

Current stack you mentioned:
- Serving on k8s with autoscaled GPUs (mixed T4 and A10 instances)
- Running an open Llama variant (float16) via an internal Python service
- A small Redis layer used for session metadata but not for KV/prefix caching

Success criteria for a pilot (as discussed):
1) Reduce per-token inference cost by ~30–40% without degrading prompt-level accuracy for core flows.
2) Keep P95 latency for production queries under ~200ms (90% of traffic).
3) Demonstrate a safe quantization path (int8/4) with an evaluation checklist and rollback plan.
4) Show how caching/batching changes map to actual $/1000-requests impact.

Where we think Redwood can help (high level):
- Autoscaling + workload-aware batching that respects your concurrency constraints.
- Prefix / KV caching for repeated contexts (recommendations & sessions).
- Quantization guidance and quality regressions monitoring tied to your prompt set.
- Concrete cost scenarios (attached spreadsheet) showing token-level economics across model variants and quant profiles.

Next steps we agreed to:
- I’ll share the cost scenarios workbook (attached) and a short checklist for the technical deep-dive.
- Schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra/ML engineer (proposed: Thu Nov 12 — 10am PT).
- You’ll share current inference cost export and a sample of ~500 prompt/response pairs for quality checks.

Attachments: redwood-cost-scenarios.xlsx

If I missed anything or got something wrong, flag it and I’ll update. Otherwise I’ll send a calendar invite for Thu and include the agenda.

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@corelytics.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya.singh@corelytics.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 18:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — inference economics, caching/batching expectations & quantization tolerance

Hi Karthik — thanks for the clear write-up. A few quick clarifications and items from our side: 

- Correct on unit economics growth — most of that is driven by two new features (search boosting & realtime suggestions) that are customer-visible.
- We are open to quantization for non-critical models (search reranker is higher risk than suggestions). The priority is keeping business KPIs (NDCG/CTR) within 1–2% of baseline.
- Regarding caching: we can add a KV cache in front of the service but need guidance on consistent cache keys given our dynamic prompts (session + short-term context).

Action items from Corelytics:
- I’ll send our current inference cost export (attached: corelytics-current-inference-costs.csv) and a small sample of production prompts (~500) by EOD Tue.
- Maya (cc’d) will join the technical deep-dive — she owns infra and throughput.

Timeline: we want a validated POC plan by end of Q1 2027, ideally with a clear cost/latency tradeoff graph we can present to the exec team.

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Patel | Head of Product 
Corelytics Inc.
sam.patel@corelytics.com | +1 (415) 555-0233

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@corelytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — inference economics, caching/batching expectations & quantization tolerance

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Sam.

We got your cost export — thanks. A couple of notes ahead of Thu’s session: 
- We’ll walk through three cost scenarios in the workbook: (A) conservative batching + prefix caching, (B) integer quantization + conservative caching, (C) aggressive quantization + batch tuning. Each scenario shows per-1000-request cost and expected p95 impact.
- For KV/prefix caching, we’ll propose a canonical key strategy that layers session-id + prompt-hash and a short TTL for freshness. We’ll also show hit-rate sensitivity (how hit-rate affects $/req).
- On quantization: we’ll run an automated eval on your sample prompts (A/B against baseline float16) and produce a short checklist (performance, hallucination rate, metric deltas). If any critical flows are impacted, we recommend model pinning for those routes.

Agenda for the deep-dive (10am PT Thu Nov 12):
- 10:00–10:15: Goals & success criteria alignment (Karthik / Sam)
- 10:15–10:45: Architecture review & caching/keying strategies (Marissa / Dev)
- 10:45–11:15: Quantization experiments and evaluation plan (Marissa)
- 11:15–11:30: Pilot scope, timeline, and next deliverables (Karthik)

I’ll send the calendar invite now with the doc and workbook attached. Marissa / Dev will lead the technical walkthrough.

Attachments: redwood-cost-scenarios.xlsx

Best,
Karthik

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Discovery recap — inference economics, caching/batching expectations & quantization tolerance

Karthik — I’ll take point on the quantization evaluation and the caching key proposal. Dev, can you bring any latency profiles and the current autoscaler config to the call? I want to map expected batching windows to realistic concurrency patterns.

I’ll prepare a short checklist we can run during the POC:
- Baseline perf and accuracy metrics for target prompts
- Quantization A/B results + metric deltas
- Cache hit-rate targets and TTL sensitivity
- Cost delta per 1% hit-rate improvement

Will share the checklist in the drive doc before the call.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
